title: Understanding KDE Plots
text: Kernel Density Estimation (KDE) is a way to estimate the probability density function of a random variable. The choice of kernel can affect how the data is smoothed.

title: Normal Kernel Characteristics
text: The normal kernel tends to smooth data in a way that can make multimodal distributions appear unimodal. This is because it assumes data is normally distributed.

title: Choosing the Right Kernel
text: Which kernel might be more appropriate for visualizing multimodal data?

title: Impact of Kernel Choice
text: Different kernels can highlight different features of the data. For multimodal data, a kernel that doesn't overly smooth the data is preferable.
